claim_assessments.claim: Layer 0 embeddings strictly isolate the edited atom; no graph-based propagation has occurred yet.
claim_assessments.reason: Results show Layer 0 dist=1 mean rel change is exactly 0.0 (std=0.0) across all models, consistent with input-layer behavior where only the modified token embedding changes.

claim_assessments.claim: Pretrained GRASP learns message passing that propagates edits across >6 bonds by Layer 8-12, whereas Random models do not.
claim_assessments.reason: At L12, Pretrained dist>=6 rel_change is ~0.48 (std=0.005) vs Random ~0.05. The gap (~9x difference in magnitude of signal propagation to distant atoms) confirms learned long-range mixing.

claim_assessments.claim: The CLS token aggregates local edits into global representations, but does not linearly track MW/LogP changes after Layer 8 in Pretrained models.
claim_assessments.reason: Pretrained L12 CLS correlation with MW is -0.016 (near zero), contrasting with Random (-0.57) and early layers, indicating learned global mixing decouples edit signal from simple size proxies.

claim_assessments.claim: Propagation decay flattens in deep layers of Pretrained models (L8+), suggesting global mixing dominates over local distance-based attenuation.
claim_assessments.reason: Gap between dist=3 and dist>=6 narrows significantly from L4 to L12 (ratio ~2.0 at L4 vs ~1.1 at L12 for Pretrained), indicating flattening of decay profile.
